tutorial.site_code: Code used to easily identify the archaeological operation. The code must be unique for the manager and is mandatory. It is limited to 32 characters.
tutorial.site_name: Full name of the archaeological operation. The name is limited to 255 characters. There must not be another archaeological operation with the same name in WEBSITE_NAME.
tutorial.site_project: If the archaeological operation is part of a project (a collection of sites, regional horizons, and other shared reference data made available to multiple users), you can select it here.
tutorial.site_region: Select the region to which the archaeological operation belongs, in order to facilitate its classification. If the region is not listed, leave this field empty or contact the admin to have it added.
tutorial.site_latitude: Enter the latitude in decimal format, using a dot as the decimal separator (e.g. 12.345); precede the latitude with a "-" if it is a southern latitude.
tutorial.site_longitude: Enter the longitude in decimal format, using a dot as the decimal separator (e.g. 12.345); precede the longitude with a "-" if it is a western longitude.
tutorial.site_descr: Free-text description of the archaeological operation. You can apply basic formatting. The current editor is still under development and may generate bugs. To format part of the text, select it and then click on the desired formatting option. To remove existing formatting, click somewhere in the formatted text and then click the corresponding formatting button.
tutorial.site_counting: Counting methods applied to your inventory.
tutorial.site_public: Indicates if the archaeological operation should be accessible for everyone or only manager and contributors of the operation and project. An archaeological operation can be public, with specific site-horizons and contexts private.
tutorial.site_unpublished: Indicates whether or not the data entered into PROJECT_NAME are published. Once the archaeological operation has been added, you can add bibliographic references. An archaeological operation can be globally published, with specifi site-horizons and contexts unpublished.
tutorial.site_biblio_review: Check this box if the data displayed for the archaeological operation are extracted (with or without revision) from a publication (generally by another author).
tutorial.site_allow_graphs: If this box is checked, any user with access to this archaeological operation can use these data to perform statistical analyses and seriation studies.
tutorial.phase_code: Code used to easily identify the site-horizon. The code must be unique within the archaeological operation and is mandatory. It is limited to 32 characters.
tutorial.phase_name: Full name of the site-horizon. The name is limited to 255 characters. The uniqueness of this name within the archaeological operation is not checked.
tutorial.phase_horizon: If you want to link the site-horizon to an existing regional horizon, choose this particular horizon in the list.
tutorial.context_phase: By default, the site-horizon within which you added the context. You can change it.
tutorial.phase_horizon_strength: Importance of the site-horizon within the regional horizon. A major assemblage defines the horizon. A minor assemblage belongs to the horizon without being fully characteristic of it. An uncertain affiliation indicates a site-horizon that probably belongs to this regional horizon, although this cannot be established with certainty.
tutorial.phase_descr: Free-text description of the site-horizon. You can apply basic formatting. The current editor is still under development and may generate bugs. To format part of the text, select it and then click on the desired formatting option. To remove existing formatting, click somewhere in the formatted text and then click the corresponding formatting button.
tutorial.phase_public: Indicates whether you want the site-horizon to be accessible to everyone, or only to the main users and contributors of the project and/or archaeological operation. A site-horizon can be public even if one of its contexts is private.
tutorial.phase_unpublished: Indicates whether or not the data entered into PROJECT_NAME are unpublished. Once the site-horizon has been added, you can add bibliographic references specific to it. A site-horizon can be published, while one of its contexts may remain unpublished.
tutorial.phase_biblio_review: Check this box if the data displayed for the site-horizon are extracted (with or without revision) from a publication (generally by another author).
tutorial.context_code: Code used to easily identify the context. The code must be unique within the archaeological operation and is mandatory. It is limited to 32 characters.
tutorial.context_name: Full name of the context. The name is limited to 255 characters. The uniqueness of this name within the archaeological operation is not checked.
tutorial.context_descr: Free-text description of the context. You can apply basic formatting. The current editor is still under development and may generate bugs. To format part of the text, select it and then click on the desired formatting option. To remove existing formatting, click somewhere in the formatted text and then click the corresponding formatting button.
tutorial.context_public: Indicates whether you want the context to be accessible to everyone, or only to the main users and contributors of the project and/or archaeological operation.
tutorial.context_unpublished: Indicates whether or not the data entered into PROJECT_NAME are unpublished. Once the context has been added, you can add bibliographic references specific to it.
tutorial.context_biblio_review: Check this box if the data displayed for the context are extracted (with or without revision) from a publication (generally by another author).
tutorial.object_number: Inventory number used to identify the artifact. This number does not necessarily have to be a number, but it must be unique within the context and limited to 128 characters.
tutorial.object_category: Abbreviation for the artifact category. If there is a corresponding category in WEBSITE_NAME, the abbreviation will be displayed in black, otherwise in grey. Maximum 16 characters.
tutorial.object_category_litt: If bibliographic review, category as published in the original publication. Maximum 128 characters.
tutorial.object_function: Name for the artifact function. If there is a corresponding function in WEBSITE_NAME, the name will be displayed in black, otherwise in grey. Maximum 128 characters.
tutorial.object_function_litt: If bibliographic review, function as published in the original publication. Maximum 128 characters.
tutorial.object_type: Name for the artifact type. If there is a corresponding type in PROJECT_NAME, a link will be added to the type page. Maximum 128 characters.
tutorial.object_type_var: If this is a variant of the type, indicate it here (preferably using the abbreviation "var.", maximum 8 characters).
tutorial.object_type_doubt: If there is any doubt about the type identification, indicate it here (preferably using the punctuation mark "?", maximum 16 characters).
tutorial.object_type_litt: If bibliographic review, type as published in the original publication. Maximum 128 characters.
tutorial.object_fabric: Code for the artifact fabric. If there is a corresponding fabric in PROJECT_NAME, a link will be added to the fabric page. Maximum 64 characters.
tutorial.object_fabric_litt: If bibliographic review, fabric as published in the original publication. Maximum 128 characters.
tutorial.object_stamp: Information about stamps present on the artifact. Maximum 255 characters.
tutorial.object_n_rim: Number of rims belonging to this artifact (optional; must be a positive integer).
tutorial.object_n_bottom: Number of bases belonging to this artifact (optional; must be a positive integer).
tutorial.object_n_handle: Number of handles belonging to this artifact (optional; must be a positive integer).
tutorial.object_n_wall: Number of walls belonging to this artifact (optional; must be a positive integer).
tutorial.object_n_mni: Minimum number of individuals represented by this artifact (based on rims alone, taking into account joins and similarities between rims). Optional; must be a positive integer.
tutorial.object_n_sherd: Total number of fragments belonging to this artifact (optional; must be a positive integer).
tutorial.object_diameter: Diameter of the artifact (specify the unit of measurement; maximum 16 characters).
tutorial.object_comment: Free-text comment on the artifact, maximum 255 characters.
tutorial.picture_name: Name used to identify the picture. Not widely used for the time being. It is nevertheless mandatory and limited to 255 characters.
tutorial.picture_type: Category of picture. Useful for sorting and characterising pictures. If other categories are required, please contact the admin.
tutorial.picture_comment: Short description of the picture, generally displayed as a caption. It is limited to 255 characters.
tutorial.picture_biblio_reference: After entering the first characters, select the bibliographic reference from which the picture originates, if it is not an original picture.
tutorial.picture_biblio_emplacement: Information about the location of the picture within this bibliographic reference (pagination, figure number, etc.).
tutorial.picture_storage: Choose whether you want to add the illustration to PROJECT_NAME or refer to an illustration hosted elsewhere (please be aware of copyright restrictions!).
tutorial.picture_url_path: For external illustrations, please provide the path to the picture. If the illustration was previously stored in WEBSITE_NAME, the file name will be displayed.
tutorial.picture_extension: Please indicate your file extension. Mandatory when uploading to WEBSITE_NAME.
tutorial.user_counting: Select the counting methods you want to be displayed in the consulted inventories (provided that these methods were used during the inventory process).
tutorial.user_is_beginner: Check this box if you want to use the simplified display (more information is provided through tooltips to help you understand how the site works).
tutorial.project_code: Code you wish to assign to your project. The code cannot exceed 16 characters, cannot be 'LOGACer', and may only contain letters, numbers, hyphens and underscores (_).
tutorial.project_name: Name you wish to give your project. The name cannot exceed 128 characters.
tutorial.project_descr: Short free-text description of the project, displayed on the project presentation page. You can apply basic formatting. The current editor is still under development and may cause bugs. To format part of the text, select it and then click on the desired formatting option. To remove existing formatting, click somewhere within the formatted text and then click the corresponding formatting button.
tutorial.project_horizon: Check this box if you wish to define regional horizons within your project, grouping similar phases (then referred to as site horizons) into a coherent facies.
tutorial.project_horizon_adv: Check this box if you wish to add data on the importance of types within the project and perform seriation studies and comparative analyses of site-horizons, contexts or regional horizons.
tutorial.project_litterature: Check this box if you wish to add original identifications of categories, functions, types and fabric groups to data taken from previous publications. These original data can be accessed via a small 'book' icon next to the standardised name of the category, function, type or fabric group.
tutorial.project_graphs: Check this box if you wish to perform graphical analyses of the finds.
tutorial.project_archaeometry: Check this box if you wish to add archaeometric analyses to the artefacts included in your project.
tutorial.project_notes: Check this box if you wish to allow users to leave personal notes or notes addressed to the authors and contributors of the records included in the project.
tutorial.project_notes_pub: Check this box if you also wish to allow notes to be left below records for anyone viewing them.
tutorial.project_img_icon: Small image (16x16 or 32x32px) displayed in the navigation tabs. To share an image, you can upload it to an external server (for example, a cloud drive). Then copy the link allowing the image to be displayed here.
tutorial.project_img_band: Image displayed in the LOGACer navigation bar, at the top left. To share an image, you can upload it to an external server (for example, a cloud drive). Then copy the link allowing the image to be displayed here.
tutorial.project_img_logo: Image displayed in the project list. To share an image, you can upload it to an external server (for example, a cloud drive). Then copy the link allowing the image to be displayed here.
tutorial.project_img_footer: Image displayed at the bottom of the page (affiliated or funding organisation, etc.). You can add up to five images. To share an image, you can upload it to an external server (for example, a cloud drive). Then copy the link allowing the image to be displayed here.
tutorial.project_link_footer: If you wish to add a link from the image to a website, enter it here. This is different from the link to the image itself.
tutorial.apptext_content: You can apply basic formatting. The current editor is still under development and may cause bugs. To format part of the text, select it and then click on the desired formatting option. To remove existing formatting, click somewhere within the formatted text and then click the corresponding formatting button. You can also insert Markdown text by checking the corresponding option to access advanced formatting features.
tutorial.comment_descr: You can apply basic formatting. The current editor is still under development and may cause bugs. To format part of the text, select it and then click on the desired formatting option. To remove existing formatting, click somewhere within the formatted text and then click the corresponding formatting button.
tutorial.facies_code: Code used to easily identify the regional horizon group. The code must be unique and is mandatory. It is limited to 32 characters.
tutorial.facies_name: Full name you wish to give to your regional horizon group. The name must be unique and is mandatory. It is limited to 255 characters.
tutorial.facies_project: If the horizon group is part of a project (a collection of sites, regional horizons and other shared reference data elements used collectively by several users), you can select it here.
tutorial.facies_descr: Free-text description of the horizon group. You can apply basic formatting. The current editor is still under development and may generate bugs. To format part of the text, select it and then click on the desired formatting option. To remove existing formatting, click somewhere within the formatted text and then click the corresponding formatting button.
tutorial.facies_public: Indicates whether you want the horizon group to be accessible to everyone or only to the managers and contributors of the project and/or horizons. A horizon group can be public while one of its regional horizons remains private.
tutorial.facies_unpublished: Indicates whether the data entered into PROJECT_NAME are published. Once the horizon group has been added, you can add bibliographic references.
tutorial.horizon_code: Code used to easily identify the horizon. The code must be unique within the horizon group and is mandatory. It is limited to 32 characters.
tutorial.horizon_name: Full name you wish to give to your horizon. The name is mandatory and limited to 255 characters.
tutorial.horizon_superhorizon: If this is a sub-horizon of another horizon within the group to which it belongs, indicate the main horizon here.
tutorial.horizon_descr: Free-text description of the regional horizon. You can apply basic formatting. The current editor is still under development and may generate bugs. To format part of the text, select it and then click on the desired formatting option. To remove existing formatting, click somewhere within the formatted text and then click the corresponding formatting button.
tutorial.horizon_dating: Dating information for the regional horizon (free-text). You can apply basic formatting. The current editor is still under development and may generate bugs. To format part of the text, select it and then click on the desired formatting option. To remove existing formatting, click somewhere within the formatted text and then click the corresponding formatting button.
tutorial.horizon_public: Indicates whether you want the regional horizon to be accessible to everyone or only to the managers and contributors of the project and/or the horizon group.
tutorial.biblio_abbreviation: Unique abbreviated name of the reference. Ideally, this name should take the form "Author date", "Author & Author date", or "Author et al. date". In the case of similar references, add a letter to the date (a, b, c...). Maximum 128 characters.
tutorial.biblio_reference: Full bibliographic reference. You can apply basic formatting. The current editor is still under development and may generate bugs. To format part of the text, select it and then click on the desired formatting option. To remove existing formatting, click somewhere in the formatted text and then click the corresponding formatting button.
tutorial.biblio_onicer_link: If this reference is included in BIBCer, enter its identifier here (the identifier only, not the full link).
tutorial.typology_code: Code used to easily identify the typology. The code must be unique and is mandatory. It is limited to 64 characters.
tutorial.typology_name: Full name you wish to give to your typology. The name must be unique and is mandatory. It should preferably make the subject easy to identify: category, period, geographical scope. It is limited to 255 characters.
tutorial.typology_project: If the typology is part of a project (a collection of sites, regional horizons and other shared reference data elements used collectively by several users), you can select it here.
tutorial.typology_descr: Free-text description of the typology. You can apply basic formatting. The current editor is still under development and may generate bugs. To format part of the text, select it and then click on the desired formatting option. To remove existing formatting, click somewhere within the formatted text and then click the corresponding formatting button.
tutorial.typology_public: Indicates whether you want the typology to be accessible to everyone or only to the managers and contributors of the project and/or the typology.
tutorial.type_code: Code used to easily identify the type. The code must be unique and is mandatory. If there is no risk of ambiguity, it is preferable to choose a code close to the name while allowing the type to be sorted alphabetically (01, 02 instead of 1, 2, for example, if there are two-digit types). For ambiguous types, an indication of the category or typology may be useful. For these reasons, it can be up to 255 characters long.
tutorial.type_name: Name of the type. It is mandatory, and different types cannot have the same name within the same category (see the links between typology and category). It is limited to 128 characters.
tutorial.type_supertype: If this is a subtype of another type within the typology to which it belongs, indicate the main type here.
tutorial.type_descr: Free-text description of the type. You can apply basic formatting. The current editor is still under development and may generate bugs. To format part of the text, select it and then click on the desired formatting option. To remove existing formatting, click somewhere within the formatted text and then click the corresponding formatting button.
tutorial.type_dating: Proposed dating for the type (free-text). You can apply basic formatting. The current editor is still under development and may generate bugs. To format part of the text, select it and then click on the desired formatting option. To remove existing formatting, click somewhere within the formatted text and then click the corresponding formatting button.
tutorial.type_onicer: Check this box if this is a type present in ONICer.
tutorial.fabric_code: Code used to easily identify the fabric. The code must be unique and is mandatory. It is the first information displayed in inventories. Ideally, if it is not linked to a main fabric, the presumed or known geographical origin should be inferable from the code. Also consider its alphabetical sorting when choosing this code. It is limited to 64 characters.
tutorial.fabric_name: Full name of the fabric, displayed on its record. The name must be unique and is mandatory. It is limited to 255 characters.
tutorial.fabric_project: If the fabric is part of a project (a collection of sites, regional horizons and other shared reference data elements used collectively by several users), you can select it here.
tutorial.fabric_superfabric: If this is a subgroup of another fabric, indicate the main fabric here.
tutorial.fabric_descr: Free-text description of the fabric. You can apply basic formatting. The current editor is still under development and may generate bugs. To format part of the text, select it and then click on the desired formatting option. To remove existing formatting, click somewhere within the formatted text and then click the corresponding formatting button.
